premise: At 57 I raided my $112,000 retirement lump sum to buy and restore a century‑old antique carousel with my brother, who promised me 40% of the ride’s earnings in a notarized memo; once the carousel appraised at $1.3 million, he forged a sole‑ownership title, sold it to a theme park, and tried to buy me off with a $4,000 ‘finder’s fee.’ I found the original memo in our late mother’s papers, proved the fraudulent transfer, and the court awarded me the entire sale proceeds—I now lease the carousel to festivals as ‘Painted Ponies & Perjury,’ and my brother must dress as the ticket‑taker clown, his earnings garnished, while a banner reads ‘The Merry‑Go‑Round of Justice.’
